item.title: Wildfires rage, force evacuations in western U.S., Canada amid drought
item.description: More than 40 large wildfires are burning in the West, fueled by severe drought, as over 100 blazes scorch parts of western Canada.

item.title: Trump says U.S. "semi-negotiating" with Iran after Tehran sets new demands
item.description: President Trump signaled he would be piling economic pressure on Tehran as the stalemate continued and Iran laid out new conditions to re-open the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Eye Opener: Firefighters battle blazes in the West
item.description: Wildfires are raging in the western U.S. and Canada as firefighters battle multiple blazes. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Undersea power cable diverted after "Harry Potter" fans complain
item.description: The CEO of Etchea Energy described being inundated with calls after inadvertently planning an underground cable beneath a memorial to the fictional "Harry Potter" character.

item.title: Taylor Farms recalls jalapeño items at Walmart, Target over salmonella risk
item.description: The recalled product with jalapeño were distributed at national retailers, including Walmart and Target, in 26 states.

item.title: London police seize record $10 million in supercars in one weekend
item.description: One of the vehicles impounded was a Ferrari Monza SP2, which can sell for as much as $5 million at auction.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strikes deep inside Russia kill at least 13, authorities say
item.description: The death toll is one of the highest among Russian civilians in recent months, as Ukraine seeks to disrupt Russia's oil supply.

item.title: Man who allegedly arranged Tupac Shakur's 1996 killing going on trial in Las Vegas
item.description: The man who prosecutors say orchestrated the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, Duane "Keffe D" Davis, is scheduled to go to trial almost 30 years after the drive-by shooting in Las Vegas.

item.title: Former Thai lawmaker arrested after allegedly shooting government official
item.description: The alleged attack came just days after a school shooting in the same region in which, authorities said, a gunman killed at least eight people.

item.title: Inside the new rise of trading cards
item.description: Interest in trading cards jumped during the pandemic, with folks digging through boxes in closets and garages to keep themselves busy. The industry is now worth an estimated $50 billion, but questions are rising about whether some of the more popular aspects of trading and collecting are actually gambling. Jarred Hill reports.

item.title: Fighting loneliness by filling empty chairs
item.description: When it comes to loneliness, sometimes the best medicine is just having someone to talk to. A global movement is bringing strangers together with a simple message: pull up a chair. Tina Kraus reports.

item.title: Mother, 5-month-old die in New York Harbor after boat capsized; captain arrested
item.description: A 46-year-old man was arrested on reckless endangerment charges, and authorities are investigating whether the boat was an illegal charter.

item.title: Wildfires in western Canada force more than 20,000 people to evacuate
item.description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said an 80-year-old woman died while trying to escape a wildfire that forced evacuations in the Okanagan Lake region.

item.title: Prison inmates train service dogs, changing lives of people they've never met
item.description: At a state prison in Stockton, California, some inmates train service dogs that will go on to help people with disabilities. Max Darrow has the story.

item.title: Taiwan practices war games as it fears increasing Chinese aggression, questions Trump's support
item.description: Taiwan continued its 10-day war games this weekend, preparing for a potential invasion by China, which claims the territory as its own and has threatened to seize it by force. Anna Coren has more details from Taiwan.

item.title: Winning Powerball numbers drawn for $863 million jackpot
item.description: The total is also the eighth-largest Powerball jackpot in the game's history.

item.title: Powerball prize increases to $905 million
item.description: The Powerball jackpot powered up after there was no winner this weekend. The prize for Monday's drawing is now an estimated $905 million, the biggest jackpot this year.

item.title: Gas prices stubbornly stuck, up more than $1 since war with Iran started
item.description: The cost of the war with Iran on taxpayers continues to grow, not only to finance the Pentagon's plans, but at the pump. Taurean Small has more.

item.title: Iran says strait won't open until the U.S. "corrects" behavior
item.description: The United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi National Oil Company said one of its ships was targeted while transiting the strait.

item.title: Iranian leaders demand U.S. pay for war damage or will keep Strait of Hormuz closed
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard insisted that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the U.S. complies with a list of demands, including paying for war damage. Imtiaz Tyab reports on the latest in a series of mixed messages from the regime.

item.title: Fires grip western U.S., British Columbia: "It doesn't seem like it's real"
item.description: Nearly 100 large wildfires strained firefighting resources around the U.S. this weekend. The fire danger also exploded in Canada amid hot and dry conditions. Gwen Baumgardner reports, and Andrew Kozak has the forecast.

item.title: Mother, 5-month-old baby killed in New York boat capsize, captain arrested
item.description: The captain of a boat that overturned in New York Harbor was charged with reckless endangerment. Twelve people were saved, but a mother and her 5-month-old daughter died. Michael George reports.

item.title: Don Nelson, former NBA coach and 5-time champion as a player, dies at 86
item.description: Don Nelson was one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with three different franchises — Milwaukee, Dallas and Golden State.

item.title: 8/9/2026: Generally Recognized as Safe; Growing Up Behind Walls; Hoosier Hysteria
item.description: First, a report on how GRAS fuels the rise of ultraprocessed foods. Then, a look inside author Mitch Albom's Haiti orphanage. And, Indiana Hoosiers: from outcast to undefeated.

item.title: Hall of Fame NBA coach and Celtics great Don Nelson dies at 86
item.description: Don Nelson, a legendary Hall of Fame basketball coach for four NBA teams and a Celtics great, died at 86 on Sunday.

item.title: 8/9: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Wildfires rage in Canada and the western U.S.; 2 were killed from a capsized boat in New York Harbor.

item.title: Bhattacharya says "I trust the science" on childhood vaccines
item.description: Dr. Jay Bhattacharya, director of the National Institutes of Health, said "I trust the science" on vaccines as measles cases have risen to their highest levels in 35 years.

item.title: Suspected Irish crime boss extradited from Dubai
item.description: Daniel Kinahan, 49, faces charges of directing an organized crime group.

item.title: Sanders calls on Democratic leaders to ban "corrupt" super PAC donations
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders highlighted the hundreds of millions of dollars spent by outside organizations during the 2026 midterm cycle.

item.title: 8/9: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Sen. Bill Cassidy joins to discuss his pivotal vote to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general. Plus, Sen. Bernie Sanders and National Institutes of Health Director Dr. Jay Bhattacharya join.
